stories.title: Insulin product in short supply after German manufacturer halts supplies, NA told
summary: An insulin product used by patients with Type 1 diabetes is in short supply in Pakistan after its German manufacturer halted supplies while upgrading its products, Parliamentary Secretary for Health Nelson Azeem said on Friday.

She said the alternatives were at least 20 per cent more expensive and that many patients did not have access to doctors. “Currently, around 34.5 million people in Pakistan have Type 1 diabetes, including children,” she said. “Alternatives are not readily available.

In August 2025, the Pakistan Medical Association raised alarm over “an unprecedented” and severe shortage of essential medicines across the country and warned that the crisis threatened the lives of millions of patients.

stories.title: DPM Dar arrives in Istanbul ahead of R-4 bloc, European diplomats’ meetings
summary: Dar left for Istanbul earlier in the day and is attending the meeting at the invitation of Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan.
The FO added that during his one-day visit, Deputy Prime Minister (DPM) Dar would participate in the R-4 and R-4-plus meetings with France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom.

A Turkish diplomatic source also told Reuters a day earlier that the seven countries would meet in the R-4+E-3 format for the first time at Turkiye’s initiative as wars involving Iran, Yemen and Ukraine threaten shipping routes and regional security.

stories.title: New Greece law bans social media for under-15s
summary: Greece’s parliament passed a law on Friday banning children under 15 from social media, joining a growing number of countries imposing curbs on young people’s use of the apps.

Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis announced plans for the ban in April, taking to TikTok — one of the most popular social networks with young people in Greece — to explain the “difficult but necessary” measure.
The opposition socialist Pasok party abstained after seeking an alternative bill that would have banned social media for under-13s and parental controls for 13- and 14-year-olds.

stories.title: China orders 'all-out' rescue after Tibet quake kills 16
summary: China ordered an “all-out” rescue effort in Tibet on Friday after an earthquake killed at least 16 people, injured dozens and flattened hundreds of homes, state media reported.
The disaster came little over a year after at least 148 people died in a quake in remote Gansu province in northwest China in December 2023, according to state media.
That quake was China’s deadliest since 2014, when more than 600 people perished in the southwestern province of Yunnan.

stories.title: West Bank attack wounds 5 Israelis as Netanyahu cancels events
summary: An attack in the occupied West Bank wounded at least five Israelis on Friday and triggered a shootout that left two Palestinians dead, prompting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to cancel political events days ahead of elections.
No evidence suggests that the Palestinian Authority, the Palestinian government in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, was connected to Friday’s attack.
The incident comes as tensions soar in the West Bank, including over attacks by extremist Israeli settlers against Palestinian olive harvesters, and days ahead of Israeli elections.

stories.title: Lahore tops global pollution ranking as air quality turns ‘hazardous’
summary: Lahore ranked as the world’s most polluted city on Friday, with its air quality classified as “hazardous”, according to air quality monitoring platform IQAir.
Lahore topped the list of the world’s most polluted cities on Friday morning, with an air quality index (AQI) of 410, according to the IQAir live tracker.
Lahore air quality map. —IQAir The Punjab government’s air quality monitoring platform, meanwhile, recorded an AQI of 339 for Lahore at 11am on Thursday, classifying the air as ‘very unhealthy’.

stories.title: Taiwan shuts down ahead of Typhoon Champi, nearly 1,000 flights cancelled
summary: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, and though the storm is weakening it could still make direct landfall on the island.

At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191 kph near its centre, according to Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration (CWA).

A fisherman walks among fishing nets at a fishing port as Typhoon Champi approaches Taiwan, in Keelung, Taiwan on October 23, 2026. —Reuters The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights were cancelled for Friday, along with 717 international ones.

stories.title: PCB opens direct signings window for PSL teams, announces pre-season roadmap
summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Friday opened the direct signings window for all eight HBL Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchises and unveiled the pre-season roadmap for the 12th edition of the tournament, which will be held from March 18 to May 2 next year.
PCB Chairman Mohsin Naqvi described the upcoming season as the league’s most ambitious edition yet. “HBL PSL is Pakistan cricket’s biggest stage, and Season 12 will be its most ambitious yet.

We look forward to a season that takes this league further than it has ever gone.” The announcement builds on the landmark 2026 season, when the PSL expanded to eight teams with the inclusion of Hyderabad Kingsmen and Rawalpindiz.

stories.title: 'Generational rage': Young Europeans fight to be heard
summary: From blockaded schools in Rome to tent camps in Madrid and street protests in France, young people across Europe are turning their anger on a political class they say is not listening.
In Italy, one student slogan last week urged protesters to “do as in France”, while shared symbols, including the Jolly Roger pirate flag, have become common across youth rallies.

An 18-year-old, who did not want to be named, said the media and politicians in Italy were focusing too heavily on looting and vandalism by some protesters. “It turns hatred against the students who are victims of this system,” he said.

stories.title: How are Ukraine strikes, Mideast war driving US fuel prices?
summary: Ahead of next month’s midterm US elections, Donald Trump has increasingly blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for surging energy prices back home, which are causing the president political headaches.

But “the impact of previous drone strikes (by Kyiv) on global product prices before the Middle East crisis was minimal”, James Henderson, a researcher at the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, told AFP.
For now, however, the strikes continue. “There’s not much that can be done in the very short term to lower diesel prices,” said Jorge Leon, an analyst at Rystad Energy.

stories.title: Utilities in Rawalpindi barred from digging up roads without permission
summary: Commissioner Rawalpindi Salman Ghani issued the directive at a meeting held to review road-cutting permissions and the installation and management of underground utility lines by various government departments.
He said all concerned departments must ensure comprehensive planning and effective coordination before undertaking any road-cutting activity.
All restoration work, including refilling and reconstruction, must be completed within 15 days of road cutting, he said.

stories.title: Proposed amendments to Islamabad LG law cast doubt on Dec 20 polls
summary: The report on the Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government (Amendment) Bill, 2026 (Ordinance No. II of 2026), was presented by committee chairman Raja Khurram Shahzad Nawaz of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) during Thursday’s session of the National Assembly.
The government introduced the bill in March this year, but the committee’s report was presented a day after the ECP announced the election schedule.

The federal government continued to postpone elections, citing various reasons, including proposed amendments to the Local Government Act, depriving around 2.5 million Islamabad residents of an elected local government system.

stories.title: ATC indicts PAF officer’s murderer, summons witnesses
summary: ISLAMABAD: An Anti-Terrorism Court (ATC) on Thursday indicted an accused arrested in connection with the murder of Group Captain Asim Tariq, and summoned prosecution witnesses to record their statements.
Judge Abual Hasnat Mohammad Zulqarnain of the ATC conducted the hearing, during which the accused, Saad Abbasi, was produced before the court.
Police have registered a case against the accused at Margalla Police Station in connection with the murder.

stories.title: Growers critcise PTB for failing to purchase surplus tobacco
summary: The sources said PTB’s role in handling tobacco affairs is critical, but its officials always toe the line of companies, leaving the poor growers high and dry.
However, they said the companies were adopting delaying tactics or were not at all interested in buying the surplus tobacco from growers.
Iqbal Khan Shewa, the association’s patron-in-chief, told Dawn that both companies and traders exploited the weak financial position of tobacco growers.

stories.title: Illegal shops, business centres razed in Charsadda, Lakki Marwat
summary: Also, an anti-encroachment operation has been launched in Tangi tehsil under the supervision of assistant commissioner Akhlaq Ahmad and additional assistant commissioner Adan Zahid to reclaim land.
Traders complained about the operation in Sherpao Bazaar, claiming that their shops were demolished without prior notice, causing them serious financial issues.

Deputy commissioner Shahid Rafiq Gandapur led the operation wherein anti-encroachment squad of the tehsil municipal administration removed illegal buildings and structures from both sides of the busy Peshawar-Karachi Highway in the Serai Gambila Bazaar.

stories.title: Delayed filing of ownership statements: Lahore High Court annuls SECP penalties on mill directors
summary: The SECP had fined each director Rs60,000 under the Securities Act, 2015, for a 253-day delay in filing Form 5 after their re-appointment.
The judge also noted that an SECP clarification of April 20, 2022, indicated ambiguity over whether Form 5 applied to re-appointment of the same directors.
The judge allowed the appeals and set aside the orders of the SECP and its appellate bench.

stories.title: Seven suspects gunned down in Karachi ‘encounters’
summary: According to officials at the Taimuria police station, a team of the Shaheen Force signaled two riders of a motorcycle to stop for checking near the DC Office in North Nazimabad, but they opened fire and tried to speed away.
They were chased along the road running parallel to the DC office, the police said, adding that in the ensuing encounter, both the suspects were shot dead.
The Korangi police also claimed to have shot dead two suspected criminals in an ‘encounter’.

stories.title: Couple shot dead in coach near Sukkur; two held
summary: SUKKUR: A couple who had contracted a free-will marriage were shot dead in a passenger coach on the National Highway near the VIG Gate, within the limits of the Baiji Sharif police station in Panu Aqil, Sukkur district, on Thursday evening.
Acting on information, Baiji Sharif police reached the spot and arrested two suspects, Abdul Malik Samejo and Abdul Hanan Samejo, along with a repeater shotgun.
A free-will affidavit dated Sept 28, 2026, identifies a woman named Sidra, daughter of Abdul Hakeem Samejo, and gives details of her previous marriage to a man named Abdul Hanan.

stories.title: Faisalabad rickshaw drivers protest against LPG overcharging
summary: TOBA TEK SINGH: Scores of rickshaw drivers staged a protest demonstration at the District Council Chowk in Faisalabad on Thursday against alleged overcharging and black-marketing of LPG cylinders.
ACCIDENT: A minor child died after a speeding car ran him over near the Millat Road Chowk in Faisalabad.
The child, identified as Arbaz, was critically injured and shifted to the Allied Hospital where he died.

stories.title: In-custody suspect killed in ‘encounter’ in Lahore
summary: A police official claimed that the CCD team was taking the suspect, identified as Noor, for the recovery of looted items when his armed accomplices opened fire on the police.
Resultantly, the suspect was allegedly killed by the firing of his own accomplices, the police official claimed.
The police official claimed that the suspect was involved in several criminal activities.

stories.title: Tensions with Karachi Metropolitan Corporation flare as railways calls in armed personnel from other cities
summary: The KMC alleged PR policemen assaulted the City Wardens director before taking him to the railways police station.

Although the City Wardens director was released after hours of talks between the two sides, the KMC high-ups moved the Sharea Faisal police to lodge an FIR against the PR police officials for kidnapping and assaulting their officer.

In separate letters to senior Pakistan Railways police officials in the two cities, the department has asked them to release a certain number of personnel “along with arms and ammunition” for deployment in Karachi.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz calls for accountability in partnerships with international consultants
summary: The prime minister welcomed Briggs and reiterated Pakistan’s willingness to open its economy to promising international markets and consult globally recognised economic experts, according to the PMO.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif met with Mr. Peter Briggs, the Managing Director, North American Operations of Alvarez & Marsal (A&M), an International Consulting Firm in Islamabad today.
Briggs thanked PM Shehbaz for the meeting and extended his gratitude regarding the government’s commitment to attracting FDI and engaging constructively with international economic experts.

stories.title: Residents write to CM Murad, urge halt to construction on Karachi's Nehr-i-Khayyam
summary: Clifton Neighbourhood Association seeks disclosure of project documents, an independent drainage study and EIA; demands restoration of waterway to its original width At the meeting, the residents again raised their objections and sought answers from the project representatives.

They called for the complete project report, approved engineering drawings, details of the engineering firm and responsible engineers, and the PC-I, including the project scope, cost and approvals, to be made publicly available.

Residents stressed that a project involving proposed changes to a major urban waterway must be supported by a proper environmental assessment, independent technical studies and transparent public consultation before any irreversible changes are made.

stories.title: Carrick under pressure as Brighton eye Liverpool
summary: Beset by infighting and off to their worst league start for decades, Manchester United host Bournemouth needing to snap a seven-game winless run to quell talk of another mid-season managerial change.
At the other end of the table, Manchester City aim to extend their flawless start to the season at Aston Villa, despite doubts over the club's future in the English top-flight.

"We have to have this hunger inside of us to keep going and never be satisfied -- to keep pushing." City face Villa Park demons Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club.

stories.title: PSX slides more than 1,330 points amid Saudi Arabia-Houthi conflict
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) remained under pressure through the first half of Friday’s session, with the benchmark KSE-100 Index sliding 1,335.01 points, or 0.81%, to 162,589.30 by the Friday prayers break, according to PSX data.
Intensified fighting between Saudi Arabia, the world’s largest crude exporter, and Yemen-based Houthis has lifted international oil prices, with Brent trading near multi-month highs around $113–114.

Analysts noted that while the session remains open for the second half, the combination of elevated oil prices and regional uncertainty is likely to keep sentiment fragile unless fresh positive developments emerge.

stories.title: Barcelona eye Clasico statement against Real Madrid
summary: By contrast Real Madrid have won four consecutive matches, thrashing RB Leipzig on Wednesday, and starting to look, for the first time since Jose Mourinho's arrival this summer, like a team.
Last season Madrid won the first meeting against Barcelona but Vinicius Junior's outraged reaction at being substituted pulled apart the fragile seams of Xabi Alonso's new era.
Barcelona have averaged over four goals a game this season and Raphinha is the league's top scorer, with 12 goals, three more than Kylian Mbappe has scored for Real Madrid, with Yamal third on eight.

stories.title: Balochistan Assembly defers move to abolish Sardari system
summary: Deputy Speaker Ghazala Gola, who presided over the sitting, announced that, in recognition of the late lawmaker’s services to the province, the assembly would adopt a condolence resolution and defer all other business until the next sitting.

Adopts resolution paying tribute to late education minister Maulana Hidayatur Rehman Baloch moved a motion seeking the postponement of the assembly’s proceedings until Monday, Oct 26, in recognition of the late former MPA’s services.

Presenting the condolence resolution, Mr Baloch said the house expressed deep grief and sorrow over the death of Sardar Nisar Ali Hazara, a former member of the Balochistan Assembly, who passed away on Oct 20.

stories.title: Labour federations oppose Pakistan Mineral Development Corporation's privatisation
summary: Speaking at a press conference and protest demonstration at the Quetta Press Club on Thursday, Mr Sultan urged the federal and provincial governments to withdraw the proposal and consult labour federations and workers’ representatives before taking any further action.
He vowed to continue the constitutional, legal and democratic struggle to protect workers’ rights.

stories.title: Three terrorists killed as forces foil attack in Gwadar
summary: GWADAR/QUETTA: Security forces killed three terrorists and foiled an attack on an unoccupied construction company camp in Gwadar, officials said on Thursday.
Security sources said forces had surrounded several other suspected terrorists near a hotel, and an operation was underway to thwart another attempted attack.
The law and order situation in the BP-250 area and its surroundings was under control following timely action by security forces and relevant intelligence agencies, the statement said.

stories.title: PSL 12 roadmap sets stage
summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Friday opened the direct signing window for the 12th edition of the Pakistan Super League (PSL), with the tournament scheduled to run from March 18 to May 2, 2027.

The board has also aligned its domestic competition calendar with the PSL pre-season schedule, with the National T20 Gold and National T20 Silver tournaments set to serve as key platforms for identifying talent ahead of the auction.

The direct-signing window marks the start of preparations for franchises as they assemble their squads for the 2027 season, with player signings, trades and retention decisions expected to shape the teams ahead of the January auction.

stories.title: Microsoft develops AI tool that can diagnose 'sequentially' like a doctor
summary: Microsoft researchers say an AI tool that diagnoses patients step by step, as doctors do, was more than twice as accurate as general physicians at solving complex medical cases, according to a study published on Thursday in Science.
Existing medical AI models typically take an all-at-once approach that examines all of a patient's symptoms, lab results and imaging studies to generate a diagnosis.
With the orchestrator coordinating the steps to reaching a diagnosis, the AI model first decides what to ask about the patient’s history and what is significant in the physical exam.

stories.title: Rybakina into Ningbo quarter-finals
summary: World number one Elena Rybakina reached the quarter-finals of the Ningbo Open on Thursday on her return from injury when opponent Polina Kudermetova retired.
Rybakina, 27, won the US Open for her third Grand Slam crown in September and usurped Aryna Sabalenka as world number one in New York.
But after beating France's Diane Parry in straight sets in the previous round in Ningbo, the world number 20 came up against a far sterner test in Shnaider.

stories.title: PCB rejects PSL salary cut proposal
summary: A proposal to reduce Pakistani players’ salaries in the Pakistan Super League (PSL) has been rejected by the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB), following a virtual meeting with franchise owners on Thursday.
During the meeting, one franchise owner argued that players’ salaries were too high and should be reviewed.
The board set January 13 as the deadline for player retentions, prompting another franchise owner to suggest that the process be held in December instead.

stories.title: Fissures take a toll on PTI internal discipline
summary: Ms Yousafzai, however, had a heated exchange with PTI interim chief Barrister Gohar Ali Khan and Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, which led to her quitting the WhatsApp groups.
A source told Dawn that Senator Yousafzai was among the party leaders who expressed a lack of trust in the PTI leadership over its failure to secure the release of Imran Khan.

PTI leader Sheikh Waqas Akram said Mr Naqvi had resigned, but Barrister Gohar rejected his resignation. “I hope that situation will be controlled as he [Firdous Shamim Naqvi] has not left any Whatsapp group of the party,” he added.

stories.title: National Assembly proceedings succumb to lack of quorum, again
summary: State Life Insurance Company After Question Hour, the National Assembly passed the Life Insurance (Nation­alisation) (Amend­ment) Bill, 2026.
The bill provides for the federal government to establish a company, to be known as State Life Insurance Company Limited, under the Companies Act, 2017 (XIX of 2017).
It states that the appointment of the company’s chief executive officer and board of directors will be made in accordance with the State-Owned Enterprises (SOE) Act and the Companies Act, 2017.

stories.title: From tech giants to anonymous nonprofits, the biggest donors in US midterms
summary: Also Read: Trump’s new AI-powered website says president lost 2020 election One Nation, a Republican nonprofit group, gave almost $138 million to the SLF.

The American Action Network, another Republican dark money group, has contributed over $64 million to the Republican Congressional Leadership Fund, which is the SLF's counterpart for electing Republicans to the House.

Other big donors on the list are billionaire businessman Jeff Yass, who has donated $109 million so far, mostly to Republican groups, as well as hedge fund manager Paul Singer, who donated over $52 million, also to Republican groups.

stories.title: Pakistan, EU flag security risks tied to Afghanistan
summary: The Afghanistan reference in the statement followed more explicit language in the joint communiqué issued after the eighth Pakistan-EU Stra­tegic Dialogue in Islamabad on June 1.

The reference is, moreover, significant because Pakistan has repeatedly urged international partners to press Afgha­nistan’s Taliban authorities to prevent terrorist groups from using Afghan territory to launch attacks across the border.

The language used in EU statements, while expressing concern on the terrorism threat from Afghanistan, indicates continuity with the latest dialogue reaffirming common ground between the two sides on the security risks associated with Afghanistan.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court bars arrest of KP Assembly deputy speaker
summary: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) has restrained the authorities from arresting Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly Deputy Speaker Suriya Bibi until Nov 10, while allowing her to retain access to her official residence.

The court fixed Nov 10 for the next hearing of Ms Bibi’s petition against the sealing of her official residence and her anticipated arrest under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.

The lawyer also cited Section 27(2) of the act, which provided that the deputy speaker could not be arrested, detained or confined, and that her official residence could not be searched, entered or raided by a law enforcement agency during her term in office.

stories.title: Houthi attacks on Saudi sites claim four more lives
summary: Meanwhile, in a televised speech, the Houthi military spok­es­person, Yahya Saree, claimed attacks on Aramco facilities in the Red Sea city of Yanbu and on the defence ministry in Riyadh.

Hormuz attacks Meanwhile, the IRGC said on Thursday that four vessels involved in illegal oil transfers in the northern Persian Gulf were simultaneously hit and caught fire after being tracked by its forces on Wednesday.

Warning for pilgrims Separately, Pakistan’s Ministry of Religious Affairs has urged pilgrims to either use Iranian carriers or verify “every Iran-Iraq air sector before departure” when travelling between Iran and Iraq.

stories.title: US, South Korean officials see little chance of Trump-Kim meeting this year
summary: United States and South Korean officials see the chances fading of a meeting between President Donald Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un this year, according to five people with knowledge of the situation.

South Korea's intelligence agency told lawmakers late last month that there was a 50% chance of Trump and Kim meeting on the sidelines of the November 18-19 summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation group in Shenzhen, China.
"President Trump in his first term held three historic summits with North Korean Leader Kim Jong Un that stabilised the Korean Peninsula," said a White House official on condition of anonymity.
